title: Canonical composition comparison for unbounded ringed-topos direct images
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], carrying sheaves of commutative rings $A,B,C$, respectively. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)$ and $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E),C)$ be morphisms of ringed topoi: their underlying functors are adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, the inverse images preserve finite limits, and the structural ring maps are $f^{-1}B\to A$ and $g^{-1}C\to B$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], direct image has underlying abelian direct image with the target-ring action induced by these structural maps. Write $D(A),D(B),D(C)$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $Rf_*,Rg_*,R(gf)_*$ for the total right derived direct images computed with K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Let $Q$ denote localization of cochain complexes of $A$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\kappa_{g,f}:R(g\circ f)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*.$$
Its normalization is as follows: for a K-injective complex $I$ of $A$-modules and a K-injective resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ of $B$-module complexes, the map $g_*f_*I\xrightarrow{g_*j}g_*J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and its class is $\kappa_{g,f,QI}$ under the canonical resolution identifications. These identifications and the comparison are natural in the derived argument.

proof.text: Construct additive tensor pullbacks adjoint to the supplied module direct images of f and g, preserving K-flat complexes with flat terms and inverting quasi-isomorphisms between them. This is the supplied-functor interface proved in the new pullback lemma.

On each homotopy category use K-flat complexes with flat terms as the resolving class. Every complex admits a resolution by the existing proved live-universe theorem CochainComplex.exists_isKFlatResolution in Sheaf.Algebra.Homology.KFlatResolution (the live specialization of the cited resolution statement). The pullback lemma gives preservation of this class and inversion of its weak equivalences. Lift the ordinary adjunctions termwise by CategoryTheory.Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategory.

Prove the needed hom-set comparison directly using the right-fraction calculus. For a K-flat test object K and a K-injective I, maps K to f_*I in the homotopy category are in bijection with maps QK to Q(f_*I). Represent a localized map by a right fraction, refine its denominator by a K-flat resolution, and use the ordinary adjunction and the bijectivity of localization into I to remove that denominator. Equality of fractions is treated by their common refinement. The Lean helper hom_localization_bijective implements both directions. The K-injective hom bijection and fraction calculus are the existing Mathlib APIs, not new assumptions.

For a K-injective I and a K-injective resolution j:f_*I to T, test Q(g_*j) by maps from every K-flat complex K with flat terms. The preceding hom comparisons for g^*, f^* and their composite identify postcomposition with Q(g_*j) with postcomposition with Qj after adjunction. Since Qj is invertible, this operation is bijective. Every derived object is isomorphic to the localization of such a K, so Yoneda implies Q(g_*j) is invertible, hence g_*j is a quasi-isomorphism. No claim that f_*I is K-injective is made.

Obtain K-injective resolutions of module sheaves from the Grothendieck-abelian theorem. For every additive functor use the existing right derivability structure on K-injective complexes to construct its right derived functor and its comparison, invertible on K-injectives. A quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence, which every additive functor preserves. These constructions use WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.Defs and Mathlib derivability APIs directly.

Choose R(gf)=Rf followed by Rg, and define its unit by eta_g(f_*M) followed by Rg(eta_f(M)). Naturality is a direct composition calculation. At a K-injective I the unit eta_g(f_*I) is invertible: choose j as above and use naturality of eta_g, the invertibility at T, and the quasi-isomorphism g_*j just proved. The K-injective derivability criterion then proves that the composite is right derived. Take kappa to be the identity isomorphism. Naturality at j and cancellation of Qj give exactly the required resolution formula. The right-derived universal property proves uniqueness from the unit equation.

lean.statement:
theorem ringedToposDerivedPushforwardComposition
    {C D E : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D] [SmallCategory E]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    (L : GrothendieckTopology E)
    (A : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (B : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{u})
    (R : Sheaf L CommRingCat.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
      RingCat.{u})).obj
      A))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
      RingCat.{u})).obj
      B))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
      ((sheafCompose L (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
      RingCat.{u})).obj
      R))]
    (f : RingedToposMorphism.{u} (C := C) (D := D) (J := J) (K := K)
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj A)
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj B))
    (g : RingedToposMorphism.{u} (C := D) (D := E) (J := K) (K := L)
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj B)
      ((sheafCompose L (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) :
    ∃ (Rf : DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂
      CommRingCat.{u}
      RingCat.{u})).obj
      A)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
            ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj
            B)))
      (Rg : DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose K (forget₂
        CommRingCat.{u}
        RingCat.{u})).obj
        B)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
            ((sheafCompose L (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj
            R)))
      (Rgf : DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂
        CommRingCat.{u}
        RingCat.{u})).obj A)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
            ((sheafCompose L (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj
            R)))
      (ηf : f.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ Rf)
      (ηg : g.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ Rg)
      (ηgf : (f.modules ⋙ g.modules).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ Rgf),
      Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηf
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂
            CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj A)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      Rg.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηg
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose K (forget₂
            CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj B)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      Rgf.IsRightDerivedFunctor ηgf
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂
            CommRingCat.{u}
            RingCat.{u})).obj A)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ (I : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
        RingCat.{u})).obj A)) ℤ),
        I.IsKInjective → IsIso (ηf.app I) ∧ IsIso (ηgf.app I)) ∧
      (∀ (T : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
        ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
        RingCat.{u})).obj B)) ℤ),
        T.IsKInjective → IsIso (ηg.app T)) ∧
      ∃! κ : Rgf ≅ Rf ⋙ Rg,
        (∀ (M : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
          RingCat.{u})).obj A)) ℤ),
          ηgf.app M ≫ κ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj M) =
            ηg.app ((f.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M) ≫
              Rg.map (ηf.app M)) ∧
        ∀ (I : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u}
          RingCat.{u})).obj A)) ℤ),
          I.IsKInjective → ∀ (T : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u, u, u, u} ((sheafCompose K
            (forget₂
            CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj B)) ℤ),
          T.IsKInjective →
          ∀ (j : (f.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I ⟶ T),
          ∀ [QuasiIso j],
          QuasiIso ((g.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map j) ∧
          ηgf.app I ≫ κ.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.obj I) =
            DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map
                ((g.modules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map j) ≫
              ηg.app T ≫ Rg.map (inv (DerivedCategory.Q.{w}.map j) ≫ ηf.app I)
